**Reported parameter record · adopted 24 October 2026 under [#215](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/215) · record `00e77608…` · Engine `3e83e19c` · [Download exact parameters](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json)**

These are electrolyte PC-SAFT (ePC-SAFT) parameters for aqueous MEA–CO₂, with nine liquid species (CO₂, MEA, H₂O, MEAH⁺, MEACOO⁻, HCO₃⁻, CO₃²⁻, H₃O⁺, OH⁻) and five reactions R1–R5. A7 is the seventh amendment of the joint-recalibration plan in [#170](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170); the current record is its [#212 refit](results/engine-3e83e19c-refit-chain/README.md), with MEA association volume 0.036305439.

The [pressure-transfer study for issue #261](composition-transfer/pressure-transfer-261.qmd) records the fixed-parameter concentration diagnosis and local data-role probes for the future #255 refit. These local fits do not change the adopted parameter record.

# Adopted record and result {#working-record}

The adopted record fits 16 adjustable parameters to 307 objective rows, using native equation-of-state densities without empirical volume translation. The common calibration subset has average absolute relative deviations of 11.86% for 47 pressures and 7.10% for 94 species targets; the eight fitted Vinjarapu heats have a root-mean-square error of 1.84 kJ/mol CO₂. Of 47 fitted loaded densities, 44 meet twice their row-specific scales, and the other three are the permitted misses at 353.15 K. The largest absolute CO₂-free density error is 0.5575 kg/m³. One of four heat-capacity points exceeds the 3% comparison limit; all four pass the numerical interpretation checks.

The [phase search](results/engine-3e83e19c-phase-search/run-2/README.md) completes 162 states per fit, over 313.15–393.15 K and loading $10^{-5}$–0.6 mol CO₂/mol MEA, at 0.50, 0.80 and 0.95 of the reported-fit bubble pressure. It resolves no descent for the reported record. This finite search does not establish global stability. The [six computed limits](results/engine-3e83e19c-density-free/limits.json), density rule, complete assessments, curve checks and [307-row replay identity](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/replay-identity.json) pass. Single local fits, active bounds and conditional uncertainty do not establish parameter uniqueness, independent physical validation, concentration transfer or absorber/stripper qualification. Independent delivered review and manuscript generator/prose updates under #211 remain pending.

## Water ideal-gas calorics {#water-ideal-gas}

The new water record replaces the extrapolated 500–1700 K Shomate function with a fit over 273.15–400 K to the ideal-gas part of [IAPWS R6-95(2018), equation 5 and table 1](https://iapws.org/documents/release/IAPWS-95.download) (Zotero `Y3FU9CXJ`). Its maximum relative heat-capacity error on 10,001 grid points is $6.50\times10^{-7}$, below the 0.001 limit. Maximum absolute errors relative to the transformed reference are $1.09\times10^{-4}$ J/mol in enthalpy and $3.35\times10^{-7}$ J/(mol K) in entropy. These are numerical fit errors, not physical uncertainty. The 501-point fit, verification grid, coefficients and replay are retained in [water-ideal-gas](water-ideal-gas/fit.json).

![Relative ideal-gas water heat-capacity error against IAPWS-95. The two panels have different vertical scales; the old record is extrapolated below 500 K. These curves compare correlations and do not show measurement uncertainty.](water-ideal-gas/cp-error.png)

The reference transformation sets $h^\circ(298.15\,\mathrm K)=-241826$ J/mol, the existing record's formation-enthalpy convention, and $s^\circ(298.15\,\mathrm K)=188.834$ J/(mol K) at 0.1 MPa, from [NIST-JANAF H-064, 298.15 K row](https://janaf.nist.gov/tables/H-064.html) (Zotero `CWCVM9IE`). At other temperatures the reference adds the IAPWS ideal-gas heat-capacity integral, or its integral divided by temperature, to the respective anchor. The old Engine record evaluated to $-241825.473101$ J/mol and $188.835269$ J/(mol K) at the anchor, so the replacement changes those offsets as well as heat capacity.

Using the fixed parameter record `00e77608…` and pinned Engine `3e83e19c`, the maximum change in the four Hilliard predictions was 0.00190 J/(mol K), compared with their 1.59–1.76 J/(mol K) declared 2% scales. Across eight Vinjarapu and fourteen Arcis integral-heat predictions the largest difference was $8.45\times10^{-9}$ J/mol CO₂. The Kim finite-addition comparison produced 73 paired values with a maximum difference of $4.15\times10^{-11}$ kJ/mol CO₂; 13 points exceed the retained loading ceiling. The 313.15 K reference-caloric heat was 83.7170 kJ/mol CO₂ for both records at the reported precision. Individual results and statuses are in [comparison.json](water-ideal-gas/comparison.json).

Relative to the retained source heat uncertainties, the largest absolute change is $8.93\times10^{-12}$ of the reported uncertainty among the 22 Vinjarapu and Arcis observations. The largest change among the 73 admitted Kim intervals is $2.15\times10^{-11}$ of the source's ±2.2% molar-heat uncertainty. These effects are negligible compared with those uncertainties for these observations and conditions, and are at numerical precision. Arcis reports a statistical estimate with unspecified coverage and possible mixing bias; the 2% Hilliard and heat uncertainties are separate from any assigned fitting scales. The [row-level ratios](water-ideal-gas/uncertainty-comparison.json) retain the uncertainty basis and units.

At 313.15 K the isolated water ideal-enthalpy contribution to R1 and R2 changes by +1.0571 J/mol reaction, and that to R3, R4 and R5 by +0.52855 J/mol reaction, using the declared reaction directions. These are component contributions, not complete reaction enthalpies: the Engine's reaction-reference completion and other species also enter the full thermochemistry.

These are fixed-parameter comparisons, not an independent physical validation or a refit. Near-zero heat differences are at numerical precision and should not be interpreted as measured effects. The fitted water record is limited to 273.15–400 K; other temperatures require a separately supported correlation. Existing historical results retain their original inputs. The new input is intended for the subsequent stable refit; this calculation does not adopt new parameters.

# Parameters {#selected-parameters}

These tables read the [selected JSON](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json), [fit summary](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/fit-summary.json), and [conditional uncertainty](results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/conditional-uncertainty.json). Parameter point estimates use about four significant figures; conditional standard errors use two. Hover over starred fitted estimates to see their full-precision values. Full precision remains in the linked JSON and CSV records. The [input hashes](figures/a7_regression_overview/output/parameter-table-inputs.json) identify the inputs.

[Green: a fixed charge or formulation definition]{.evidence-1} · [Blue: a numerical input with recorded qualifications]{.evidence-2}. [★](#fitted-coordinates){.fit-star} identifies fitted component or pair inputs and all 16 declared coordinates. Tied diameters and transformed chemistry are described explicitly. Green does not certify fitted properties.

CO₂ has induced 2B association with water and no self-association; its cross-association inputs are in `topology.edges` of the selected file. Ion association is absent.


::: {title="Exact water-diameter constant 2.78043261494 Å; full coefficients in the selected JSON"}

Water diameter (rounded display; use the selected JSON for numerical work), with $T$ in K and $\sigma$ in Å. The constant and amplitudes are in Å; exponent coefficients are in K⁻¹:

$$\sigma_{\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=2.78+10.11 e^{-0.01775T}-1.417 e^{-0.01146T}$$

:::

The selected file uses solvent-density-temperature permittivity with the retained shared stage-5 water parameters. It excludes dispersion between ions with the same charge sign. For MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻, packing diameter is 0.88 times segment diameter and Debye–Hückel diameter equals segment diameter; Born diameters vary separately. No empirical density translation is applied. Fixed and transferred inputs carry their recorded qualifications; these tables confer no new physical validation.

For R1–R3, $\ln K=A+B/T+C\ln T+DT+\Delta$; R2 already includes the conversion in $A$ and has no separate offset. For R4, $\ln K=A+B/T$. For R5, $-\log_{10}K=A/T+B+CT$. The displayed layouts therefore give $B$ in K for R1–R4 and $A$ in K for R5; $D$ for R1–R3 and $C$ for R5 are in K⁻¹. Other coefficients are dimensionless. R2/R5 include the fitted pivot-preserving enthalpy shifts at 313.15 K; R5 also varies its unshifted source A. The displayed reaction coefficients include these transformations and are not independent fitted coordinates or new source measurements.

### Higher-temperature density probes (issue 268)

Measured loaded densities above 353.15 K exist, and 20 such Han cells were
already retained in this repository. Han et al. (2012), DOI
[10.1021/je2010038](https://doi.org/10.1021/je2010038), Tables 3–4
(pp.1097–1098), report loaded densities through 413.15 K and unloaded densities
through 423.15 K. The present model comparison stops at its declared 393.15 K
limit. Its retained Han subset contains 50 loaded and 17 unloaded cells at
30 mass % MEA on the CO₂-free solvent basis. Above 353.15 K there are 20 loaded
cells at analytical loadings 0.10, 0.21, 0.32, 0.44 and 0.56 mol CO₂/mol MEA,
and five unloaded cells. The recorded pressures are 0.1 MPa through 363.15 K
and 0.7 MPa from 373.15 K. Han's uncertainty discussion (pp.1101–1102) gives
combined loaded-density uncertainty 1.3 kg/m³ and expanded uncertainty
2.6 kg/m³ at 95% confidence. Unloaded expanded uncertainties are 0.68 and
0.70 kg/m³ below and at/above 373.15 K, respectively.

The comparison adds 24 source-checked unloaded cells from Sobrino et al.
(2016), DOI [10.1016/j.jct.2016.03.021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jct.2016.03.021),
Table 6 (pp.235–236): 293.15–393.15 K at 0.1 MPa and printed MEA mass fractions
0.1001, 0.2000, 0.3005 and 0.4000. Its standard density uncertainty is
0.35 kg/m³; Section 2.1 gives expanded uncertainty below 0.7 kg/m³ with
coverage factor 2. The comparison uses 0.70 kg/m³ as that reported upper
limit. The [source record](https://tnnrpolley21-ms-7c95.taila72856.ts.net:3000/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/src/commit/889ba3e03284442a25d8f1cd40ae6fc475758bf8/data/reference/MEA/observations/density_viscosity/README.md)
retains the table checks, composition/pressure conventions, Zotero identities
and PDF hashes. These cells have no fitting role. The 234 density comparisons
combine these cells with the previous 210, counting each source cell once.

These are homogeneous-liquid equation-of-state predictions and local
calibration probes, with no volume translation. Source expanded uncertainties
and the original 47 fitted-density residual scales remain distinct. The
existing Han assessment-only adoption is preserved. The two exploratory fits
add only the 25 higher-temperature Han cells to the unchanged 307-row
objective, using combined uncertainty as the residual scale and weights 1/20
for the 20 loaded cells and 1/5 for the five unloaded cells. These group weights
are study choices, not weights prescribed by Han. Neither fit adopts a new
parameter record or supplies an untouched prediction assessment.

The original 16-coordinate declarations retain their historical physical
bounds and size ties. Incremental reaction-enthalpy bounds are translated to
each start's inherited laws, without applying the inherited shifts twice.
The 600 s native fit limit, 180-iteration limit and original stopping tolerances
are retained. The final-start and wider-bound-start fits both converge, but
convergence is conditional on these bounds and stopping criteria; it is not
a global minimum or parameter-identifiability claim.

The [sensitivity reduction](results/density-268/sensitivity-summary.json)
compares full and half centered steps separately for each coordinate. For the
final set, increasing the constant coefficient in water's temperature-dependent
segment diameter by 0.1% (0.00278043 Å), with its exponential terms fixed,
lowers the mean higher-temperature Han density by 2.05863 kg/m³ for unloaded
rows and 2.13981 kg/m³ for loaded rows. Its maximum full-versus-half-step
derivative difference on those unloaded rows is 0.00039001 kg/(m³ Å),
compared with a mean derivative of −740.3976 kg/(m³ Å). This is local numerical
step verification. It does not assign uncertainty to water parameters.
The direction improves the positive unloaded errors while worsening negative
loaded errors. Increasing MEAH⁺ dispersion energy by 0.1% instead changes
the mean loaded density by +0.01706 kg/m³ and has an unloaded response below
0.00002 kg/m³ in magnitude. These different responses support treating neutral
packing and the reactive ionic volume response separately; they do not
identify unique single-ion volumes or statistically rank uncertain parameters.
The full file also retains MEA/water segment-count, MEA diameter,
MEA/water dispersion and MEA–water constant/slope sensitivities at both starts.
The MEAH⁺ one-segment convention remains fixed.

The [five extensions of retained #255 vectors](results/density-268/README.md#retained-255-vectors)
calculate only the missing higher-temperature Han densities. Their original
307-row scores and phase searches are reused, not repeated. Setting the final
MEAH⁺ diameter alone to the wider-bound value overshoots all 20 loaded Han
higher-temperature densities by 12.33–106.32 kg/m³; its retained fitted-density
count is 0/47. Increasing the wider-bound diameter alone to 5.35 Å
underpredicts those 20 by 19.46–93.09 kg/m³ and retains 0/47 fitted density
checks plus 24/32 detected descent states. The retained wider-bound
MEAH⁺–water constant −0.175 vector has 40/47 fitted density checks and a
complete 162-state search without descent; only 8/20 of its newly evaluated
higher-temperature loaded Han densities meet 2.6 kg/m³. The tested Born and
ion-pair moves preserve 47/47 fitted density checks but retain descent and
meet only 4/20 of the new Han checks each. The original phase results use
wheel `0d08dff9…`; these additional density predictions use the qualified
`83ede7d2…` wheel and are labelled separately.

For **#255 stage 2**, retain the current parameter adoption and use this work
as evidence for a joint density/phase fit. Keep the original 47-row requirements
and higher-temperature Han residuals visible as separate conditions; a lower
averaged objective alone hides their tradeoff. Preserve the source campaigns
and reported pressures, and keep Sobrino as an unloaded assessment series.
Use the MEAH⁺ size, dispersion and water-interaction law together rather than
changing size alone or treating 5.35 Å as an experimentally established bound.
Check neutral packing against unloaded/pure-component evidence before freeing
it to repair loaded densities: the tested water-diameter direction moves both
cohorts together despite their opposing errors. Any change to persistent Han
roles, fit weights, physical bounds or model form belongs to the stage-2 design.
Neither probe supplies a replacement parameter set. The supported conclusion
is a density conflict among the tested bounded fits with no detected descent,
not nonexistence across all admissible coordinates. Source correlations,
active parameter bounds, finite phase searches and the 393.15 K cutoff limit
transfer to absorber or other process conditions. These are calibration and
numerical-verification results, not physical validation. Independent delivered
review returned **Supported** for this bounded study and the recommendation to
#255 stage 2. No manuscript promotion is implied.

# Broader MEA heat-capacity comparison {#broader-mea-heat-capacity-comparison}

Broader heat-capacity calibration did not remove the unloaded 318.15 K discrepancy in these two bounded probes. With the corrected water ideal-gas record, the baseline error is +5.532%; probe A gives +5.531% and probe B +4.087%, compared with Hilliard's stated ±2% accuracy. Both probes converge, but fail the agreed density-preservation limits and develop dense-liquid descent. They are diagnostic endpoints and are not recommended for adoption. This result means **not removed by these tested probes**; it does not establish structural impossibility.

## Measurements and intended comparison

[Source rows](heat-capacity-264/sources.csv) and [live PDF identities/hashes](heat-capacity-264/source-provenance.json) retain 68 Hilliard measurements, six selected Weiland values and three selected Concepción values. Hilliard (2008), Appendix G.2 p.937/PDF994, provides 17 temperatures from 313.15 to 393.15 K at each of loadings 0, 0.139, 0.358 and 0.541 mol CO₂/mol MEA, with 7 mol MEA/kg water. The first three series supply 51 probe-fit observations; the 17 at 0.541 are outside this issue's loading domain. The four historical fitted observations are part of these 51, and are replaced rather than duplicated. Weiland et al. (1997), Table 3 p.1004, supplies six independent comparison rows at 298.15 K, 30 wt% unloaded analytical MEA, and loadings 0–0.5. Concepción et al. (2023), Table 3 p.3, supplies three independent unloaded comparisons at 313.15, 333.15 and 353.15 K, MEA mass fraction 0.2997 and 0.100 MPa. These sources cover selected states, not the entire temperature–loading rectangle.

Hilliard §§4.5–4.6, pp.71–78, describes sealed pans and a temperature ramp; experimental sample pressure is not reported. The assigned 101325 Pa calculation pressure is an assumption. The falsifier and phase searches are conditional on that prescribed model state, and gas descent does not establish instability in the sealed experiment. Total loaded-solution mass is used for all heat capacities. Nominally unloaded calculations retain the historical 10⁻⁶ mol CO₂/mol MEA trace feed.

Hilliard §4.6 pp.78–80 states ±2% accuracy and ±1% reproducibility; neither is identified as a standard uncertainty. The 2% residual scale continues the existing policy. Weiland's experimental section states ±1% repeatability and agreement with standards; this is a comparison band, not a statistical confidence interval. Concepción Table 3 gives 1% expanded uncertainty with coverage factor 2, corresponding to a 0.5% standard residual scale. [Nearby-composition unloaded source comparisons](heat-capacity-264/unloaded-source-comparison.csv) show Concepción above Hilliard by 4.712%, 4.511% and 4.755% at the three common temperatures. Their slightly different MEA concentrations and the unknown Hilliard pressure prevent treating this as a same-state replication, but the difference exceeds the sum of their stated 2% and 1% bands. Source agreement cannot be assumed.

Zhang, Que and Chen (2011), Table 3 p.68, gives the Aspen MEA ideal-gas polynomial over 283–1000 K, without uncertainty. The retained coefficients are translated to the existing 313.15 K-centered `IdealPolynomial` representation; the polynomial was checked against the source, not refitted here. Their §§3.1–3.3 and Tables 7 and 10 describe fitting binary and ternary caloric data with aqueous electrolyte NRTL and PC-SAFT vapor/pure-fluid properties. Baygi and Pahlavanzadeh (2015), §§3.1–3.3 and Tables 2–5, instead fits saturation/binary VLE and compares ternary pressures. Neither paper's use of a model establishes independent heat-capacity validation for these probes.

## What carries the calculated heat capacity

[Baseline decomposition](heat-capacity-264/decomposition.json) and [probe A](heat-capacity-264/probe-A-decomposition.json) / [probe B](heat-capacity-264/probe-B-decomposition.json) retain all 60 states. Frozen-composition heat capacity comes from the Engine's reference-completed `solved_state_actions` phase property. It includes the ionic caloric reference completion; a homogeneous-state total without that completion would mislabel the reaction remainder. Frozen molar quantities are multiplied by solved phase amount/feed mass, while the equilibrium observable is multiplied by feed amount/feed mass. Both are then expressed in kJ/(kg loaded solution K).

Residual constant-volume contributions use the existing MDEA diagnostic relation, $C_{v,r,t}=-R(2T a_{t,T}+T^2a_{t,TT})$, where $a_t$ is the Engine's dimensionless residual Helmholtz contribution at fixed density and composition. This is a diagnostic derivative of Engine values, not a second equation-of-state implementation. The residual pressure–volume coupling is $C_{p,r}-C_{v,r}$. Neutral ideal terms, completed source-reference calorics, residual contributions and reaction equilibration are reported separately.

At unloaded 318.15 K, the decomposition is:

| Contribution / kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ | Baseline | A | B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Neutral MEA ideal | 0.433651 | 0.433652 | 0.433661 |
| Water ideal | 1.309716 | 1.309717 | 1.309720 |
| Completed source reference | 0.000123 | 0.000123 | 0.000518 |
| Hard-chain residual Cv | -1.305965 | -1.305939 | -1.305268 |
| Dispersion residual Cv | 2.186993 | 2.186919 | 2.137581 |
| Association residual Cv | 1.261778 | 1.261782 | 1.261876 |
| Debye–Hückel + Born residual Cv | -0.000047 | -0.000047 | -0.000045 |
| Pressure–volume coupling minus R | 0.039012 | 0.039026 | 0.033414 |
| Reaction equilibration | 0.000008 | 0.000000 | 0.000056 |
| Equilibrium total | 3.925270 | 3.925233 | 3.871513 |

The water change raises the original unloaded 318.15 K prediction by only about 0.000083 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. The reaction remainder is also too small to account for the 0.205770 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ baseline difference. Probe B reduces the total by 0.053757 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, carried mainly by dispersion (−0.049412) and coupling (−0.005598); other terms partially offset that change. This locates the response to the tested residual interaction change, not a unique experimental error in one EOS term. Explaining the entire baseline difference by a uniform MEA caloric-reference shift would require approximately −41.964 J/(mol analytical MEA K); no source uncertainty or independent ideal-gas measurement here authorizes that correction. Loaded states have substantial completed-reference and reaction contributions and cannot be interpreted using the unloaded balance alone.

At 0.05 and 0.025 K derivative steps, the maximum residual-Cv closure discrepancy across all three endpoints and 60 states is 4.61×10⁻⁵ J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; the maximum term change on halving the step is 2.99×10⁻⁵ J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Closure passes the declared 10⁻⁴ relative plus 10⁻⁴ J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ absolute criterion. This is numerical verification of the decomposition, not physical validation.

## Broader fits and other-property consequences

Probe A uses the existing 14 coordinates and bounds. Probe B adds MEA–water interaction intercept and reciprocal-temperature slope, bounded ±0.05 and ±100 K about the endpoint. Both start from the selected parameter set and accepted reaction laws, keep ideal-gas calorics fixed, and replace the four Cp rows with the 51-row set. The objective therefore contains 354 observations. The 22 existing integral heats are comparison controls; they are not inserted into this objective. Both runs use the declared 60-iteration/1200-second limits and native tolerances. A converges in 31 iterations and B in 35, each with zero native trial failures. Independent endpoint replay agrees with native weighted residuals within 10⁻⁶.

## Recommendation for issue 255 stage 2

Retain all 51 in-domain Hilliard values as one source campaign for broader caloric calibration, with their pressure assumption and method accuracy explicit; do not present the 17 temperatures as independent campaigns. Keep the six Weiland and three Concepción rows as independent comparison campaigns at this selection stage, retaining the unloaded-source disagreement. Exclude the 0.541-loading Hilliard series from this issue's 0–0.5 domain. Any stage-2 expansion of those roles must preserve source bases and phase requirements.

Do not adopt A or B: both violate density preservation and develop dense-liquid descent. Neither removes the unloaded 318.15 K error below the source accuracy. The residual dispersion/coupling response explains the change achieved by B, while source disagreement and unquantified MEA ideal-reference uncertainty prevent a unique causal attribution. These are local calibration probes and conditional numerical comparisons with measured data; they do not demonstrate independent predictive validity, global non-identifiability, structural impossibility, or physical validation. Parameter adoption remains with issue 255, and this notebook has not been promoted for manuscript use.

Subsequent calculations use the corrected water record. The main checkout's pin is unchanged. # Stability-constrained refit (issue 255) {#stable-refit-255}

A refit that enforces liquid-phase stability during fitting, inside the original wide bounds, finds one stable optimum from both the final set and the wider-bound fit. It has a lower calibration cost than the final set: **148.5105** against **148.8833** for the 307 objective rows, with both on the same inputs and Engine wheel. It is a candidate only. The adopted record, Engine pin and manuscript are unchanged. MDEA shares its bicarbonate–water interaction and its R2 law; transferring both roughly doubles the MDEA pressure error, so adoption needs an owner decision.

## What was enforced

Each stability row is the Engine #1059 requirement: a Full tangent-plane search of an all-liquid parent at a pressure $c$ times the candidate's own reactive bubble pressure ($c = 1.05$ and $3.0$). It penalizes the most negative resolved reduced tangent-plane distance $\tau$. The fit enforces 1903 such states: 15, 25, 35 and 45 wt% MEA, 313.15–393.15 K, loadings $10^{-5}$ and 0.025–0.6 mol CO₂/mol MEA, plus the stage-1 census nodes. A further 576 offset states and the stage-1 162-state liquid + vapor census never enter the fit and are checked at each endpoint. The design and its qualification are in the [results README](results/stable-refit-255/README.md) and the [accepted design](results/stable-refit-255/design-probe/design.md). On the new wheel, the final set has 0 descent states and the wider-bound fit has 1207 of 1908, plus 54 of the 162 census states.

| Run | 307-row cost | Descent (enforced / offset / census) | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|---|
| final set (reference) | 148.8833 | 0 / 0 / 0 | — |
| start from final set | 148.5106 | 0 / 0 / 0 | pass |
| **start from wider-bound fit (selected)** | **148.5105** | 0 / 0 / 0 | pass |
| (a) R2 enthalpy shift held (#262) | 148.5210 | 0 / 0 / 0 | pass |
| (b) adds R4 shift and 10 Böttinger 353 K rows (#263) | 148.2631 | 0 / 0 / 0 | pass |
| (c) #261 pressure data roles (sensitivity) | 148.6884 | 0 / 0 / 0 | pass |

The two starts agree within 0.023 optimizer scales on every coordinate, so stability alone does not return the fit to the final set. The selected endpoint moves the MEAH⁺ segment diameter from the narrowed 5.35 Å bound to 4.905 Å and the carbamate diameter from 4.866 to 5.32 Å. The bicarbonate–water interaction moves from 0.727 to its upper bound of 1.0. Six coordinates end on bounds. Against the final set, the largest pressure or species rise is +0.012 AARD points (fitted phase mole fractions). Loaded densities within twice their scale rise from 44 to 46 of 47. Heat of absorption and heat capacity keep their within-2s counts, with AARD and RMSE ratios between 0.97 and 1.02 ([assessment](results/stable-refit-255/wide/assessment.json)).

The #212 conditional uncertainty, the #214 phase-family export and `generate_figure_data.py` were not rerun; they belong to adoption. The final-set rerun reproduces its retained values (state targets within $10^{-12}$; the 4 Cp rows within $2.2\times10^{-5}$, the #260 water record). The MDEA heat at 333.15 K, 60 wt% and 1.121 MPa for B1 stays unavailable under Engine #1073.

## Meaning and limits

From the final set the requirement was not binding: that fit ends with stability cost 0 and records no resolved descent along its path, so the narrowed #170/#212 bounds, not stability, held its cost (the MEAH⁺ diameter sat at its 5.35 Å bound). From the wider-bound fit (148.2156, 1207 descent states) the penalty moved the fit to the same stable optimum; relative to that unstable optimum, stability costs +0.295. A stable, lower-cost fit therefore exists inside the wide bounds. The cost gain is small (0.25 %). The concentration-transfer bias is reduced, but the transfer AARD, the 353 K carbamate excess, the 318 K heat-capacity offset and the carbonate share remain. The selected endpoint pushes the shared bicarbonate–water interaction to its bound, which harms MDEA and pushes the carbonate share further low.

This is calibration and numerical verification:
- The stability search is finite at declared states; it is not a global certificate.
- The endpoints are local optima with six coordinates on bounds.
- The acceptance rules are repository policy.

# Salt-anchored bicarbonate and carbonate interactions (issue 282) {#carbonate-ions-282}

Issue #282 tests one hypothesis: the fitted bicarbonate–water interaction (0.727 in the final set, 1.0 in the #255 candidate) compensates for an amine-solution effect. Its first step fits the water–HCO₃⁻ and water–CO₃²⁻ temperature laws to aqueous sodium-salt osmotic coefficients on this record's own water model. Its second step refits MEA with those laws held. Falsifier F1 decides whether the salt laws are an established anchor; the MEA refit runs only if it passes.

## Salt reference on the record's water

The data and model:
- **NaCl.** Hamer & Wu 1972 Table 16, 298.15 K, 0.1–1.0 mol/kg. This sets the water–Na⁺ constant, with Held's 2014 temperature slope held.
- **NaHCO₃ and Na₂CO₃.** The single-salt rows of Peiper & Pitzer 1982 Table 6, 278.15–318.15 K, 0.01–1.0 mol/kg, transcribed from the PDF page images. Each row is evaluated at its printed equilibrium ionic composition, charge-closed, with dissolved CO₂ removed as ideal.
- **Ions.** Na⁺ and Cl⁻ follow Held 2014 and the record's ion conventions. Na⁺–Cl⁻, Na⁺–HCO₃⁻, Na⁺–CO₃²⁻ and Na⁺–OH⁻ are Held's values.
- **Scoring.** The three fits run in sequence; F1 is scored on one document holding all three final laws.

![Osmotic coefficients on the ionic basis: source values (points) and the combined-document model at the same rows (lines) for NaCl, NaHCO₃ and Na₂CO₃. Right: the fitted water–anion laws over 278–393 K (fitted range shaded) against Held 2014, Wangler 2018, the final set and the #255 candidate.](results/carbonate-ions-282/salt/phi-molality.png){#fig-carbonate-ions-282}

|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| NaCl | 10 | 1.51 | water–Na⁺ $a_0$ at −1: fails "interior" | bound is a stated limit |
| NaHCO₃ | 45 | 0.163 | ≤ 1.5 %: met | ≤ 1.5 %: met |
| Na₂CO₃ | 45 | 5.11 | ≤ 1.5 %: **not met**; water–CO₃²⁻ $a_0$ at −1 | ≤ 6.5 %: met; bound is a stated limit |
| mixed NaHCO₃ + Na₂CO₃ (comparison) | 39 | 2.56 | not fitted | not fitted |

| Law | Fit | Value at 313.15 K | Comparison at 313.15 K |
|---|---|---:|---|
| water–HCO₃⁻ | $0.1117+3.93\times10^{-3}\,(T-298.15)$ | 0.171 | Held 0.00; Wangler −0.100; final set 0.727; #255 candidate 1.0 |
| water–CO₃²⁻ | $-1.000+1.96\times10^{-3}\,(T-298.15)$ | −0.971 | Held −0.25 |

**F1 as first written failed; under the owner's amendment it passes, with no fitted number changed.** As written, two fitted constants end on their lower bounds and the Na₂CO₃ AARD of 5.1 % exceeds 1.5 %. The owner amended F1 on 2026-11-09 (issue #282, "Owner amendment to F1"):
- **Na₂CO₃ limit 6.5 %.** This is the worst comparable univalent-cation/bivalent-anion case in Held 2014 Table 5, Na₂HPO₄ at 6.43 % (strategy 2, 298.15 K).
- **Bounds.** Coefficients on a bound are stated limits, not gate failures.
- **Falsification level.** The water–HCO₃⁻ ≥ 0.5 at 313.15 K test is unchanged; the fitted law gives 0.171, so it is not falsified.

Both sets of gates are retained in [salt/summary.json](results/carbonate-ions-282/salt/summary.json). **Every MEA and MDEA result below is conditional on the water–Na⁺ and water–CO₃²⁻ intercepts sitting at −1.**

## MEA refit with the salt laws held

**Leverage (no fit).** Substituting the salt laws into the final set raises its 307-row cost from 148.883 to 351.479. Moving the new MEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻ coordinate by ±0.1 changes that cost by +15.445 and −15.299, against the 0.1 threshold, almost all through the 47 fitted CO₂ partial pressures. The coordinate is therefore fitted.

**Starts and anchor.** Both substituted starts, with MEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻ = 0, were checked as retreat anchors on the 1903 enforced states and the 307 rows:
- **The substituted final set** has every state available, no resolved descent and every row available. It is the anchor.
- **The substituted #255 candidate** has two unavailable CO₂-free 25 wt%, 333.15 K states. The Engine refused its initial fit evaluation at one of them, so that start gives no candidate. No other start or fallback was added.

**Budget.** Under the owner's 3-core cap per job, the per-stage wall-time limit was scaled from 7200 s to 76 800 s for these two refits only. Both stages converged well inside it: 31 iterations in 6736 s, then 7 iterations in 1861 s.

**The fit and retreat.** Both stages end with 6 enforced states still descending. The retreat toward the anchor gives an admissible record at t = 0.975693.

The A3 and B1 MDEA records were re-evaluated with the two salt laws in place of the shared bicarbonate–water and carbonate–water values. Their MDEA-specific parameters were not changed.

The pressures are overpredicted at nearly every row. The MDEA heat at A3, 333.15 K changes from −76.3 to about −49 kJ/mol, and at B1, 388.71 K from −64.1 to about −40 kJ/mol. The B1, 333.15 K heat stays unavailable (Engine #1073).

The MDEA-specific parameters were fitted with the old shared values, so this rise says they would need refitting for any new shared value. That refit is out of scope here, and the rise does not refute the salt values. The run does not separate the bicarbonate law from the carbonate law. [Full tables, coordinates and logs](results/carbonate-ions-282/README.md).

## What limits the salt fit

At 298.15 K, lowering the water–Na⁺ or water–CO₃²⁻ intercept through the five tested values (−1, −0.5, 0, 0.5 and 1), with the other coefficients fixed, raises φ toward the reference values at every sampled molality. This supports the direction toward the lower bound for those rows; it does not establish global optimality of the full temperature-dependent fit. ([scan](results/carbonate-ions-282/salt/sensitivity.json).) At the bounds:
- **NaCl** stays 1.1–1.7 % low.
- **Na₂CO₃** is already 1.1 % low at 0.01 mol/kg, where the water–CO₃²⁻ constant has almost no lever. Its deficit peaks at 8 % near 0.2 mol/kg.

This points to the 2:1 electrostatic and Born treatment on this water and to the fixed Held cross values (Na⁺–CO₃²⁻ = −1.000 is itself a bound value in Held 2014) rather than to the water–anion constants. That is an inference; no term-by-term decomposition was run. Held's ion parameters were fitted with a different water (Fuchs 2006), and the Na⁺/Cl⁻ Born diameter is a design choice without a source.

The salt-reference design is unchanged; under the amendment these bounds are carried as limits.

## Meaning and limits

A stable MEA record exists with salt-anchored water–HCO₃⁻ and water–CO₃²⁻, and it passes the #255 acceptance rules without the fitted bicarbonate–water value of 0.727. The compensation moves to MEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻, which the fit drives to its +1 bound, and several other MEA-ion coordinates move by several optimizer scales. The record costs 1.2 more than the final set and moves the shared MDEA pressures far from their data.

Limits:
- **Evidence type.** This is calibration against model-derived salt reference values (Peiper & Pitzer's Pitzer tables) and the 307 MEA rows. It is numerical verification, not validation, and it establishes no physical MEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻ value.
- **The refit** is a local optimum from the one admissible start. The stability search is finite at declared states, and the acceptance rules are repository policy.
- **Temperature range.** The salt laws are fitted at 278–318 K and extrapolated to 393 K.
- **Bounds.** Every result is conditional on the two salt-fit intercepts at −1.
- **Unchanged files.** The parameter record, the Engine pin and the manuscript are unchanged.

Whether MDEA follows any new shared value remains the owner's decision.

## Bicarbonate and carbonate: source spread and bounded probes {#bicarbonate-carbonate-266}

At 30 wt% MEA and 293.15 K, the accepted parameter record falls inside the Matin–Böttinger pooled-species envelope at 18 of 19 matched loadings, separately at 101325, 500000 and 2500000 Pa. Two converged bounded probe fits preserve every fitted-group criterion but still cover only 18 of 19 points. The remaining point is loading 0.531 mol CO₂/mol analytical MEA. Its atmospheric pool is 0.0105036 mol/mol true liquid at baseline and about 0.010514 after either probe, below the envelope's lower value of 0.0114. Thus source disagreement covers most tested states, but it does not cover every state. These two local probes do not establish an unrestricted structural impossibility or a new adopted parameter set.

### Sources, conditions and quantities

Matin 2012, Method Description and Results/Discussion, pp. 6615–6617, derives speciation from titration and carbon/alkalinity balances and reports bicarbonate values above the NMR comparisons. Jakobsen 2005, Calibration Experiments and Sample Preparation, pp. 9894–9897, Table 2 and Tables A1/A2 p. 9902, separates common-peak species by calibration; its Results/Discussion warns that a species contributing below about 10% of the common signal is difficult to quantify. Böttinger 2008, §§3–7 and Table 3 p. 137, measures the common bicarbonate/carbonate signal by online NMR and fits an extended Pitzer model to speciation and vapor–liquid data. These source statements do not give a statistical uncertainty for the present inter-source difference. The reading copies and their current Zotero sources were hash-checked during reconciliation and independent readiness review. Source keys are Matin X5FACKMR/6UD2LJ7G, Jakobsen VDRXENRB/XVFDEJM2, and Böttinger E322TKPZ/TJCRKTFQ.

The [existing observation mapping](../../data/reference/MEA/manifests/speciation_linear_coefficient_rules.csv) owns the pooled quantity

$$X_{\mathrm{pool}}=x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}.$$

Here each $x$ is a true-liquid species mole fraction, in mol/mol. At each of the 19 Matin loadings 0.106–0.531 mol CO₂/mol analytical MEA, linear interpolation uses only the bracketing points in Böttinger's 12-point 30 wt%, 20 °C series. The empirical scale is the absolute difference of the two source values; it ranges from 0.000418824 to 0.008 mol/mol. The envelope is their minimum and maximum. It is not a confidence interval, a standard deviation or an estimate of the fraction of model error caused by either experiment. Reported zeros remain zeros, and no source extrapolation or logarithm of zero is used.

Matin's retained condition is 293.15 K and 101325 Pa; the paper also labels ambient comparisons at 21 °C, which remains a temperature limitation. Böttinger's individual pressures are unavailable, so its observations remain outside fitting and predictions are evaluated separately at 5 and 25 bar. Those two predictions are scenarios for the same source observations, not independent experiments. The same source envelope is compared with the model at all three pressures; it is not three pressure-matched experimental envelopes.

Jakobsen remains a separate comparison. Its nominal 30 wt% preparation contains dioxane and D₂O dilution; the retained water-equivalent translation uses unloaded MEA mass fraction 0.2714274817 and measured `loadNMR`. A three-source matched spread is unavailable without a model-dependent composition correction. The nine-species model does not describe dioxane or isotope effects explicitly. Probe 2 transfers the 20 °C empirical scale across composition only to states 010–013, at loadings 0.19, 0.29, 0.25 and 0.37. Every other Jakobsen state, including 40 °C states 018–021, remains evaluation-only; [inputs.json](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/inputs.json) records all exclusions and source rows.

Two different carbonate fractions must remain distinguishable:

$$S_{\mathrm{pool}}=\frac{x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}{x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}},\qquad
F_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}{x_{\mathrm{CO_2}}+x_{\mathrm{MEACOO^-}}+x_{\mathrm{HCO_3^-}}+x_{\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}}}.$$

Jakobsen state 011 has source pool 0.0008, $S_{\mathrm{pool}}=0.75$ and historical $F_{\mathrm C}=0.0190476$. The last follows the historical treatment of its blank CO₂ entry; that blank is not a measured zero. Baseline predictions are respectively 0.000801645, 0.0350537 and 0.000978759. The historical ten-point calculated/observed mean 0.0727222 refers to $F_{\mathrm C}$, not $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$. Common-peak calibration limitations apply to the split within that signal.

The historical Matin AARD of 67.4563% mixes sixteen pooled predictions with bicarbonate-only predictions for states 009, 016 and 019. Summing the retained bicarbonate and carbonate species consistently gives 67.4145%, which the present baseline reproduces. The maximum difference between those retained sums and the new baseline predictions is 7.1 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol/mol. This is a mapping reconciliation, not a physical improvement. [Historical pool reconciliation](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/historical-pool-reconciliation.json) retains each source file hash, both species and the legacy scalar.

### Sensitivity at fixed parameters

The Engine evaluates each positive and negative perturbation with the other parameters fixed. R2 and R3 native log-law coefficient $a$ use steps of 0.1; each interaction coefficient uses 0.01; carbonate segment diameter uses 0.01 Å, with packing/segment ratio 0.88 and Debye–Hückel/segment ratio 1 retained. Born diameter stays at 3 Å. Every fresh prediction agrees with the corresponding native coordinate evaluation within the declared numerical tolerance. The steps are diagnostic choices, not physical parameter uncertainties.

The table shows the change caused by the positive step. The Matin state is 30 wt%, loading 0.531 and 293.15 K; the separate Jakobsen state is the translated nominal-30-wt% state 015 at loading 0.78 and 293.15 K. Both model evaluations are at 101325 Pa. At state 015, baseline $S_{\mathrm{pool}}$ is 1.35695 × 10⁻⁵ versus the source value 0.0307018; the source split lies in the paper's difficult minor-carbonate range and is not fitted here.

These local responses neither identify unique parameters nor rank effects independently of step size. [All sensitivity values](results/bicarbonate-carbonate-266/sensitivity-values.csv) retain all states, both signs and central finite differences.

### Probe fits and preservation of the original objective

Probe 1 adds the 19 Matin pool observations, with difference residuals divided by the empirical scale and weights 1/19. Probe 2 additionally includes the four declared Jakobsen pool observations, each at weight 1/4; the scale transfer is conditional on the retained composition translation. The original 307 rows keep their construction parameters, observations, scales and weights. Each fit starts independently from the accepted endpoint. Only the six sensitivity coordinates move: R2/R3 $a$ within ±ln(10), the three interactions within ±0.1, and carbonate segment diameter within ±0.2 Å, with the stated diameter ties preserved.

Both fits converge in nine iterations with no trial failures. Fresh weighted residuals agree with the native fits to maxima of 1.59 × 10⁻¹¹ and 7.19 × 10⁻¹², below the 10⁻⁸ absolute allowance. Native and fresh total costs agree within the 10⁻⁸ relative allowance. All 326 probe-1 and 330 probe-2 predictions are available and meet their unchanged requested tolerances. The controls remain 60 iterations, 1200 seconds, function tolerance 10⁻⁸, parameter tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and gradient tolerance 10⁻⁸. Requested Engine workers equal the full CPU count; numerical-library threads are one. Runtime files record actual elapsed times and package/input identities; no unexposed actual worker count is inferred.

Four coordinates reach their bounds in both probes: R3 $a$ reaches 9.8432078883, carbonate–water $k_{ij}$ reaches −0.35, carbonate–MEAH⁺ $k_{ij}$ reaches +0.1, and carbonate segment diameter reaches 2.6422 Å. Bicarbonate–water $k_{ij}$ moves from 0.7270558477 to 0.7296094565/0.7296315265; R2 $a$ moves from 23.5855161421 to 23.5829717634/23.5829472822. This is boundary-limited local fitting, not an interior optimum, a covariance-based uncertainty estimate or a global search. At Jakobsen state 011 the predicted pooled split decreases to 0.00191464/0.00191455, farther from the source split of 0.75, even though the pooled mole fraction remains near the measured sum. Fitting the pooled amount therefore does not constrain the individual carbonate fraction here.

These calculations include repeated physical states from separate fitted-observation declarations; they are not 420 independent experiments or a proof of global stability. Vapor witnesses remain distinct from liquid instability, and the phase files retain each witness, support, raw residual and native message. The original-wheel baseline had one unresolved reconstruction trial; the final qualified-wheel results supersede it for this comparison, while the old evidence remains in `wheel-3e83e19c/`.

### Recommendation for issue 255 stage 2 and limits

Keep Matin's pooled minor-species observations as source-disagreement diagnostics rather than automatically adding them to the adopted calibration. Keep Böttinger outside fitting under its existing unknown-pressure ruling and retain the 5/25-bar comparisons. Keep separately calibrated Jakobsen carbonate fractions, especially high-loading minor-carbonate splits, outside fitting unless a source-supported uncertainty treatment is selected. Preserve the existing qualified major-species observations and source/campaign identities. The four extra Jakobsen pool rows tested here are composition-transfer diagnostics, not an automatic promotion to active calibration data.

For stage 2, retain the consistently pooled Matin mapping and both explicitly named carbonate denominators. Carry forward the empirical envelopes and this bounded result: most points are consistent with inter-source spread, but neither of the two declared probes reconciles the last point while representing the carbonate split. The near-identical probe endpoints and active bounds warrant no parameter adoption. This is a local diagnostic comparison with measured data and numerical replay/phase verification, not independent physical validation, parameter identification, absorber qualification or evidence that every admissible model would fail.
